item.title: Mormor or farmor? How to talk about family in Swedish
item.description: Talking about family in Swedish can be complicated. Discussing your relatives requires an in-depth knowledge of exactly how they are related to you, so it's time to start brushing up on your family history.

item.title: Is it legal for your Swedish boss to contact you out of hours?
item.description: In an ideal world, your boss would never need to get hold of you while you're on holiday or during your time off. But what does the law say if they do?

item.title: A beginner's guide to buying an apartment in Sweden
item.description: Thinking of buying an apartment in Sweden, but struggling to get to grips with the nuances the locals take for granted? Fear not, our handy guide will put you on the right path.

item.title: Sweden plans to publish bill easing rules for researchers and PhDs in March
item.description: Sweden's government has said it intends to push forward with a long-delayed plan to bring in better residency permit rules for foreign researchers and PhD students, with a bill scheduled to be published in March.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Swedes expect property prices will rise, almost half of teenage boys at risk of gaming addiction, Iranian nurse couple granted review from deportation and more news from Sweden on Monday.

item.title: 'Pig cold': How to talk about the winter weather in Swedish
item.description: Swedes are famously not fans of small talk, but if you find yourself forced into small talk with a Swede then the weather is always a safe choice of topic. It’s no surprise then that there are so many words in Swedish to talk about the cold.

item.title: Swedish foodie secrets: How to find Sweden's best semla
item.description: Semlor are traditional Swedish cardamom buns filled with whipped cream and almond paste. But what should you look for in a good semla, and what should you avoid?

item.title: Key figure in Sweden's Foxtrot gang seized in Iraq
item.description: A 21-year-old described by as "very close to the top leader" of the Foxtrot gang was arrested in Iraq in December, according to Swedish police.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: vovve
item.description: If you're raising bilingual children in Sweden, this may very well be one of their first words as soon as they start to get a sense of the world around them.

item.title: Calf dance and boiled bread: The weirdest Swedish foods to get EU protection
item.description: Sweden is battling to win Norrland and East Coast Baltic herrings EU 'Protected Designation of Origin' status ‒ joining a stable of fishy specialities that is starting to rival France's list of cheeses. But a lot of the other specialities are pretty weird. How many of these have you heard of?
